name: Delonix Performance Engine
author: delonixteam

sections.description:
Delonix Performance Engine keeps a cached copy of every public page for desktop, tablet and mobile, and sends it before PHP loads your theme. It also handles images, CSS, JavaScript and Core Web Vitals. All of it runs on your own server, so there is no account to create and no page quota.

Activate it, pick the Safe or Balanced profile, and warm the cache. The Server-Timing response header shows HIT-EARLY when a page came from the early cache.

Page cache

  • Desktop, tablet and mobile are cached separately, so a phone never gets the desktop layout.
  • An advanced-cache.php drop-in answers before WordPress boots. Apache and LiteSpeed can also serve desktop pages straight from disk (off by default).
  • Editing a post refreshes its own page and marks related archives, listings and feeds stale.
  • A preload queue rebuilds pages in small batches from your sitemap, your home page links and the pages that were purged.
  • Home, archives and products refresh sooner than static pages. While one request rebuilds an expired page, other visitors keep getting the previous copy.

CSS, JavaScript and fonts

  • Local Edge mirrors your CSS, JS and font files, minifies the CSS and JS, stores gzip and Brotli copies where the server supports them, and sends long browser-cache headers.
  • Scripts are deferred in dependency order, so jQuery plugins still find jQuery.
  • HTML minification, font-display: swap, and preconnect hints for third-party hosts the page already uses.
  • Optional link prefetch: a page is fetched when the pointer rests on its link.

Images

  • WebP copies of JPEG and PNG files, delivered in a <picture> element with the original as a fallback.
  • Missing width and height are added so the layout does not jump.
  • Broken srcset and sizes are repaired, and images below the fold load lazily.
  • The Media screen converts the existing library one image per request, and you can pause it.

Core Web Vitals from real visits

A small script records LCP, CLS, INP and TTFB from a sample of your visitors and saves them in your own database. The dashboard compares the last 7 days with the 7 days before, per device. Raw IP addresses are never stored.

Stores and members

  • Cart, checkout, account and login pages are never cached. The plugin finds them in the settings of WooCommerce, Easy Digital Downloads, MemberPress, Paid Memberships Pro and LearnDash.
  • WooCommerce order-attribution cookies (sbjs_*) do not turn the cache off for visitors.
  • Cache rules adapt when Delonix Security Agent is active.

AI agents

  • A generated /llms.txt, and an ARD manifest at /.well-known/ard.json when a plugin registers an agent resource.
  • Fast plain 404s for machine-readable files that do not exist.
  • Missing accessible names are added to icon-only links, buttons and dialogs.

Moving in

  • Import your WP Rocket settings and review each one before saving.
  • WP-CLI: wp delonix-performance has status, purge, warm, image optimization and drop-in commands.
  • A purge menu in the admin bar.

Safe and Balanced profiles

Safe is for page builders, membership sites and stores where nothing may break. It does not defer JavaScript. Balanced is the everyday setting and adds dependency-aware JavaScript defer. You can change any single option afterwards.

Delonix PE Pro

Delonix PE Pro is a separate add-on plugin. It adds critical CSS learned from real visits, JavaScript delay, learned LCP preload and AVIF. Every feature of this plugin works without it. Compare Free and Pro.

External services

The plugin does not send analytics, telemetry, RUM measurements, cache data or site content to Delonix, and it does not contact any third-party server.

Cache warmup requests are made back to the site’s own URLs through the WordPress HTTP API.

Resource hints. The Preconnect to busy third-party hosts setting adds preconnect hints only for third-party hosts that the page already loads resources from. It does not add any new third-party resources.

Admin links. The Dashboard shows a dismissible card with a link to the Delonix Security Agent page on delonix.biz, and the Settings page links to the Delonix PE Pro page. Nothing is requested from delonix.biz unless the administrator clicks a link.

Privacy

Real-user measurements stay in the site’s database. Public RUM submissions use a short-lived salted hash derived from the request IP address only as a rate-limit key; raw IP addresses are not stored in the RUM tables. The plugin does not contact Delonix for telemetry, licensing or remote code.

Local RUM is enabled by default and stores sampled Core Web Vitals, the page path, the device class and the cache state in the site database. It can be turned off with the Real-user monitoring setting. Suggested privacy policy text is added to Settings > Privacy.
sections.installation:
1. Go to Plugins > Add New, search for Delonix Performance Engine, then install and activate it. If another page cache plugin is active, deactivate that one first.
  2. Open Performance > Dashboard and apply the Safe or Balanced profile.
  3. Open Performance > Cache and select Warm cache.
  4. Check the early cache. When page cache is enabled and wp-config.php is writable, the plugin adds define( 'WP_CACHE', true ); so the early drop-in can run before WordPress boots. If the file is not writable, add that define manually before the “stop editing” line.
  5. If another plugin already owns wp-content/advanced-cache.php, Delonix Performance Engine leaves that file untouched and runs without it.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require a CDN or cloud optimization account?

No. The cache, media optimization, Local Edge and RUM features run on the WordPress installation. Local Edge is an origin-side asset cache, not a geographic CDN.

Does the plugin collect telemetry?

No. RUM measurements are stored locally in the WordPress database and are not sent to Delonix.

Why does the plugin use advanced-cache.php?

WordPress supports wp-content/advanced-cache.php as a drop-in for cache systems. When the plugin owns that file and WP_CACHE is enabled, a safe cached response can be served before the full WordPress bootstrap. The plugin enables WP_CACHE in wp-config.php when that file is writable, removes only its own marker line on deactivate, and will not overwrite a foreign advanced-cache.php. These files are written only while an administrator is using wp-admin, never on a visitor request.

Does the plugin edit .htaccess?

Only when you turn on “Serve cached pages directly from the web server” (off by default). The plugin then writes a # BEGIN Delonix Page Cache block before the WordPress block, so Apache or LiteSpeed sends fresh cached pages to desktop visitors without starting PHP. Phones, tablets, logged-in users, query strings and stale pages still go through WordPress. A one-time backup is kept as .htaccess.delonix-bak, and the block is removed when the option is turned off or the plugin is deactivated or uninstalled. On nginx the settings page shows an equivalent snippet to copy.

The rules turn themselves off while a bot gate such as Delonix Security Agent is active, because only PHP can check the gate’s cookie. Cached pages are then served by the early cache in PHP instead.

Does uninstall remove all stored data?

By default, uninstall preserves performance data and settings. Site owners who want a full cleanup can define DELONIXPE_REMOVE_DATA_ON_UNINSTALL as true before uninstalling.

What does the llms.txt feature publish?

Only public information that is already on the site: the site name and tagline, published pages, WooCommerce product categories, blog categories, the sitemap and the privacy policy page. It is generated when /llms.txt is requested and no real file exists, is skipped when search engines are discouraged in Settings > Reading, and can be changed with the delonixpe_llms_txt and delonixpe_llms_txt_sections filters or turned off in Settings.

Will the accessibility repair change my design?

No. The script only adds missing aria-label / aria-labelledby attributes and removes list, menu or tablist roles from containers that contain no matching items. It does not change visible content or styles.

Can I use it with WooCommerce?

Yes. The plugin never caches cart, checkout and account pages, and treats WooCommerce order-attribution cookies as safe so visitors keep getting cached pages. Start with the Balanced profile and test the extensions your store uses.

Can I switch from WP Rocket?

Yes. Export your WP Rocket settings, open Performance > Settings > Import and review the result before saving. Then deactivate WP Rocket, because two page caches should not run together.

How do I know the cache is working?

Open a page in a private window and look at its Server-Timing response header. MISS means WordPress built the page and HIT-EARLY means the early cache sent it. Logged-in users are never served cached pages.

Is there a Pro version?

Yes, as a separate add-on from delonix.biz. This plugin is complete without it and has no locked settings.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0

  • Initial public release.
  • Requires WordPress 6.9: page HTML is optimized through the core template enhancement output buffer.
  • AI agent readiness (llms.txt, ARD manifest support, fast 404 for machine files, accessibility-tree repair).
  • Device-separated full-page cache with an optional pre-bootstrap advanced-cache.php drop-in, URL-shaped cache folders and host-name checks.
  • Smart purging: a post update refreshes its own page and marks related listings, archives and feeds stale.
  • Preload queue fed from sitemaps, home-page links and purged pages, warmed in small batches per device.
  • WebP generation, <picture> delivery and responsive image repair.
  • Local RUM (LCP, CLS, INP, TTFB) stored only in the site database.
  • Safe and Balanced profiles, admin-bar purge menu, WP-CLI commands and a settings importer for sites moving from WP Rocket.
  • WooCommerce order-attribution cookies (sbjs_*) no longer bypass the page cache.
